parts.text: Identify how many people in the world are estimated to be homeless, from Source 1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify two causes of homelessness, from Source 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which cause of homelessness do you think is the most significant? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Using Source 3, explain one local and one national consequence of homelessness.
Local consequence: ______
National consequence: ______

text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Homeless people are spoiling our city!’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘There are more homeless people on our streets.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Identify one value judgement from Source 4. Explain why this is a value judgement.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Pia’s or Jack’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
Your local community wants to reduce homelessness in the area.
The following actions are being considered:
• fund local charities to support homeless people
• use government money to provide very cheap housing
• make it a crime to live on the streets.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the community, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
